headings.title: From a committed message to a selectable UI source
Preparation and the final dispatch check

html:
Saved assistant task-context flows

Save to task context selects an existing assistant message for later decisions in its task notebook. It retains a source reference and selection metadata, not a second copy of the message. Reading, saving and removing selections do not start inference, resume a waiting task or grant execution authority. The broader notebook and carry-forward policy is described in context and memory.

From a committed message to a selectable UI source

flowchart TD Commit[Canonical run journal commit] --> Publish[publish_sources resolves new messages] Locator[Scope-local assistant locator] --> Check[Check complete source,<br/>ownership and current access] Publish --> Check Journal[Original journal entry] --> Redact[Current output/input redaction] Check --> Redact Redact --> Text[Visible prose or question/options] Text --> Metadata[Source reference, revisions<br/>and presentation identity] Metadata --> Event[Source-available event<br/>or listing metadata] Event --> UI[Per-turn source cache] Visible[Complete visible assistant candidates] --> Hash[Hash exact candidate text] Hash --> Match[Require one source/display digest match<br/>and compatible presentation identity] UI --> Match Match --> Button[One Save action per source reference] Match -->|Ambiguous or unavailable| Omit[Remove or omit action]

saved_messages.py resolves a source through a document locator in the notebook scope. It requires a complete, eligible assistant message, checks Books access, finds the run's journal membership and loads the canonical message. Missing, transient, incomplete or revoked sources are unavailable. Scope membership and retained branch grants constrain access; sharing a conversation label is insufficient.

The resolver applies current model-output policy, then the service's current model-input projection/redaction. assistant_text selects visible final-response or ordinary assistant content and valid ask_user question/options. It does not select private reasoning or arbitrary tool-call bodies. The source revision hashes the exact projected UTF-8 text; a separate display revision hashes trimmed text. Changing current redaction can therefore change the projected source revision.

After canonical state publication, native state and decision acceptance call publish_sources. It walks new message indices after the run's publication watermark, resolves each eligible source and emits metadata without source text. It advances the watermark past examined messages, including skipped ones. These events advertise available sources; they do not save selections or issue model requests.

saved_task_context.js binds once per rendered turn using its captured request/conversation identity. It collects complete assistant rows, closed narration blocks and nonprovisional, nonbusy final text. It hashes each candidate and matches one server source/display revision, requiring equal presentation IDs when both sides supply one. Multiple matching sources are ambiguous and get no action. Duplicate rendered views of one source receive only one action in that reconciliation pass.

Hashing is asynchronous. The helper rechecks that a candidate remains attached and its text is unchanged before adding a control. A microtask coalesces render starts, but does not serialize all asynchronous draws. A source event arriving during the initial listing read is merged into that result rather than discarded. Read failures are silent and leave existing state; explicit refresh or later source events provide subsequent opportunities to update it. Disposal disconnects the DOM observer; it does not cancel in-flight reads or remove saved selections.

Save, retry and removal transactions

sequenceDiagram participant UI as Per-turn Save control participant API as Saved-context routes participant Service as Source selection service participant DB as Notebook transaction participant Broker as UI update broker UI->>API: POST source reference, revision and submission ID API->>API: Require license acceptance and resolve live task ownership API->>Service: Save selection Service->>DB: Check current notebook and submission receipt alt Identical submission already recorded DB-->>Service: Return recorded save ID without reactivation else Submission ID used for another source or revision DB-->>API: Conflict API-->>UI: HTTP 409 else New submission Service->>DB: Re-resolve live source and compare exact revision Service->>DB: Activate absent/removed selection and record receipt DB-->>Service: Committed save ID end opt Save returned successfully API->>Service: Reread current listing API->>Broker: Publish runs/chats invalidation API-->>UI: Listing and save ID end opt User removes a saved identity UI->>API: DELETE save ID API->>Service: Remove within live notebook Service->>DB: Mark removed and withdraw head reference API->>Service: Reread listing API->>Broker: Publish invalidation after commit API-->>UI: Updated listing end

The routes use /api/agent/native/{request_id}/task-context/saved-messages, with the conversation identity supplied by the client. They reject a mismatched conversation, tombstoned/deleted conversation, absent notebook or retired bound task with 404. GET lists selections; POST saves; DELETE addresses a save ID. Mutations require the current EULA gate. Source/selection conflicts become 409. The strict POST model bounds the reference and submission ID and requires a 64-character revision; the service, not those length checks, verifies identity and revision equality.

check_current verifies the run is live and belongs to this notebook. A selection made on an older message attaches to the notebook's current active epoch when its head has advanced. save executes atomically with its idempotency receipt. A submission ID hashes to a receipt key; reusing it for another source/revision is a conflict. Replaying the same receipt returns its save ID without saving again. In particular, an old retry after removal cannot restore that selection.

A new submission re-resolves the source and compares its public revision. The save ID is deterministic for the source reference. An absent or removed selection is activated and advances the notebook selection revision; an already active selection does not become a duplicate. Removal marks the item removed, drops its head reference and advances the selection revision only when that reference existed. It does not delete the underlying journal message. A deliberate new save after removal uses a new submission ID and must be delivered again.

The browser serializes mutations within each turn binding. A Save button keeps its submission ID after a failed request and clears it only after success, allowing safe retries when the response was lost. Listing and broker publication happen after the transaction. Their failure can produce an error after the selection already committed; it is not a rollback. The error panel opens and controls become available again. A response describes saved state, not the success of a later model decision.

Preparation and the final dispatch check

sequenceDiagram participant Prepare as Context preparation participant Sources as Live notebook sources participant Capacity as Context capacity owner participant Dispatch as Reserved model dispatch participant Hook as before_dispatch callback participant Transport as Provider transport Prepare->>Sources: Resolve all active selections strictly alt A selected source is unavailable Sources-->>Prepare: Unavailable IDs without copied text Prepare->>Prepare: Block before model request else Sources resolve Sources-->>Prepare: Current full projected text and selection revision Prepare->>Capacity: Assemble required context and optional progress alt Required context exceeds capacity Capacity-->>Prepare: blocked_capacity with saved IDs else Context fits Capacity-->>Dispatch: Prepared packet and required final tail Dispatch->>Sources: Check selection revision before reserved call Dispatch->>Dispatch: Reprepare changed context when supported Dispatch->>Hook: Install context-submission callback Hook->>Sources: Recheck sources, retained context, instruction and tail alt Context changed again Hook-->>Dispatch: SelectionChanged before HTTP send Dispatch->>Prepare: Retry preparation without stale submission else Context still matches Hook->>Sources: Record submitted context and inclusion receipts Hook-->>Transport: Continue provider request end end end Note over Hook,Transport: Receipt precedes HTTP send<br/>and does not prove provider success

Preparation resolves saved selections in strict mode. A revoked or missing source leaves a removable metadata identity in listing, but blocks preparation with SavedSourceUnavailable. It cannot be reconstructed from copied saved text. Every resolution reapplies current source policy and redaction; a prior successful read is not a permanent grant.

Prepared messages carry the full projected selections in a clearly labeled packet of assistant claims. That packet does not convert those claims into new user instructions or execution evidence. Optional progress reduction does not silently shorten saved messages. If required context and saved selections exceed capacity, the capacity owner reports saved_task_context_exceeds_capacity before provider work. Remove selections or use a supported capacity change before continuing.

Reserved model dispatch checks the selection revision alongside other execution-context inputs. It can reprepare changed ordinary context; an existing provider continuation follows its separate context-change rejection path. Immediately before HTTP dispatch, request_lifecycle.before_dispatch invokes the installed callback after the generation dispatch fence. submitted checks the live selections, retained generation IDs, active instruction, preceding reply and required final message against the prepared packet. A mismatch raises SelectionChanged; the model-decision owner retries preparation rather than sending that stale packet.

The callback records saved-source inclusion only when the prepared packet is present in the supplied messages. It also records overall context-delivery diagnostics and emits task_context.context_submitted. The transport calls this boundary before the HTTP send, so these receipts establish submitted composition, not provider acknowledgement, response acceptance or model comprehension. Removing a selection cannot retract bytes from a request already sent.

Displayed status and retained diagnostics

flowchart TD Selection[Current active selection] --> Resolve{Source available now?} Resolve -->|No| Unavailable[Source unavailable<br/>Keep removable identity only] Resolve -->|Yes| Compare{Receipt matches source<br/>and selection revision?} Compare -->|Yes| Included[Included in model input] Compare -->|No| Failure{Capacity error names this ID<br/>at current selection revision?} Failure -->|Yes| Blocked[Context capacity exceeded] Failure -->|No| Pending[Saved for next decision] Remove[Remove then deliberately re-save] --> Revision[New selection revision] Revision --> Compare Receipt[Retained context-delivery receipt] --> Inspector{Preparation ID matches<br/>and no current blocking failure?} Inspector -->|Yes| Submitted[Show receipt diagnostics] Inspector -->|No| Current[Keep current preparation diagnostics]

The panel shows a short preview and View saved message for the full current projection. Included in model input requires a receipt matching both source revision and selection revision. Otherwise it shows Saved for next decision, unless a current capacity failure names that selection. An old capacity error or old inclusion receipt cannot override a newer selection. Unavailable selections show a removal instruction without their revoked text.

delivery_diagnostics reads a bounded retained receipt and uses it only when its preparation ID matches and the current preparation is not reporting unavailable sources or blocked capacity. An optional consumed-retained-generation list remains a distinct observation. Desktop and mobile refresh after context-submitted or run-failed events and ingest source-available metadata through their turn bindings.

Verification references

Saved-context fixtures exercise full text, idempotent retries after removal, deliberate reselection, concurrent saves, current redaction, revoked sources, capacity failure and changes between preparation and dispatch. Their RAM/standalone fixtures use scripted model owners. The saved-message API case checks listing, save/removal, conversation mismatch and absence of a model wake. Browser fixtures exercise real desktop/mobile renderers with intercepted selection APIs and scripted trace events. They verify selectable completed progress/final messages and removal; they do not establish real provider delivery or behavior.
